# SOP-311 — Electrical Panel Lockout / Tagout Procedure

**Applies to:** All 415V and 11kV distribution panels in the process area.

## 1. When This Procedure Applies

Before any inspection, maintenance, or repair work that requires opening
a panel enclosure or exposes personnel to potential contact with live
parts, full lockout/tagout (LOTO) is mandatory. No exceptions for
"quick checks."

## 2. Standard Sequence

1. Notify affected operations personnel and identify all energy sources.
2. De-energize the circuit at the designated isolation point.
3. Apply a personal lock and tag at the isolation point — one lock per
   worker, no shared locks.
4. Verify zero energy state with a rated voltage tester before touching
   any conductor.
5. Perform the work.
6. Remove tools, confirm the panel is clear, remove locks/tags in reverse
   order, and re-energize only after a visual confirmation the area is
   clear.

## 3. Alert Thresholds Requiring Escalation

- Voltage tester reads any value above 0V after isolation and lockout —
  work must stop immediately and the isolation point must be
  re-verified with a second qualified electrician before proceeding.
- Panel enclosure temperature above 60 degrees Celsius at time of
  inspection (indicates a possible loose connection or overload).
- Any sign of arc flash damage (scorch marks, melted insulation) on
  opening the enclosure.
- Missing or illegible arc-flash warning label on the panel.

## 4. Corrective Actions

- Residual voltage detected: treat as an isolation failure. Do not
  proceed. Escalate to the electrical maintenance lead immediately.
- Elevated panel temperature: schedule thermal imaging survey and
  torque-check all connections within 72 hours.
- Arc flash damage found: panel must be de-rated to a documented safe
  operating condition or taken out of service until repaired; a formal
  incident report is required regardless of whether anyone was injured.

## 5. Approval

Only personnel currently certified for the panel's voltage class may
perform LOTO on it. Return-to-service after any Section 3 finding
requires sign-off from the electrical maintenance lead.
